title: Aspire 13.6 Adds Persistent Dashboard Telemetry and First-Party Java and Rust Hosting
gist: Microsoft released Aspire 13.6, adding SQLite-backed persistent dashboard telemetry, prerelease first-party Java and Rust hosting, and opt-in database REPLs. The release also carries several breaking changes and makes the Aspire MCP server opt-in for coding agents.

insights.claim: Aspire 13.6 ships prerelease first-party hosting for Java (executable JARs, Maven/Gradle wrappers, Spring Boot, Quarkus) and Rust (Cargo apps via AddRustApp), extending the orchestrator beyond .NET.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Microsoft is positioning Aspire as a multi-language cloud-native dev orchestrator, widening its addressable developer base.

insights.claim: The Java and Rust integrations build on work from the Aspire Community Toolkit, showing community packages being promoted into first-party support.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Community-to-first-party graduation signals an ecosystem-led roadmap.

insights.claim: TypeScript AppHosts now load appsettings.json from their own directory, and Deno 2 or later can run the TypeScript AppHost.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Aspire is investing in non-C# AppHost authoring, reducing .NET lock-in.

insights.claim: The Aspire dashboard now stores resource snapshots and telemetry in SQLite, enabling run persistence by default with up to ten runs kept per application; completed runs are read-only.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Run history makes the local dashboard a debugging record, not an ephemeral view.

insights.claim: The persistent telemetry database has no encryption or authorization layer, and Aspire sets no Windows ACLs on the data directory, so stored telemetry is only as protected as the filesystem.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Persisted logs and traces may leak sensitive data on shared dev machines; a security consideration for enterprise adoption.
insights.locator: As stated in the release notes

insights.claim: Default limits for console logs, structured logs and traces rise to 100,000 each, and the dashboard ships as a Native AOT executable on Fluent UI Blazor v5.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Higher retention and AOT packaging point to heavier local observability use.

insights.claim: Agent setup in aspire new and aspire init now leaves the Aspire MCP server unselected, making MCP opt-in rather than default.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: A shift toward conservative defaults for agent access to developer environments.

insights.claim: The Visual Studio Code extension lets coding agents start and stop AppHosts, and adds deploy and publish actions to the Aspire pane.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Aspire is being made controllable by AI coding agents, integrating with agentic workflows.

insights.claim: New WithRepl options on PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, SQL Server, Redis and Valkey open the bundled client; they use real credentials and are not read-only, so they are disabled unless a developer opts in.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Convenience features that grant write access are gated by opt-in, reflecting caution about real-credential exposure.

insights.claim: AppHosts can open their own terminals in a dashboard dock through the experimental TerminalService API.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Experimental API; early signal of dashboard-as-workspace direction.

insights.claim: Azure Connector Namespace and Azure Container Apps Sandboxes are added as preview integrations that require preview access in the Azure subscription.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Aspire is a vehicle for pulling developers toward new Azure services.

insights.claim: MongoDB resources now use TLS during local runs when a certificate is available, replacing the earlier plaintext default.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Secure-by-default local dev, but a breaking change for existing setups.

insights.claim: The Cosmos DB emulator defaults to the Linux-based vNext image, and existing classic emulator data does not carry over.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Upgrade requires data migration planning for Cosmos DB users.

insights.claim: The release removes the GitHub Models integration and changes Azure Front Door origin names on upgrade.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Removal of GitHub Models suggests a retreat from that integration while Microsoft Foundry Toolboxes are added.
insights.locator: Azure Front Door origin names change

insights.claim: AddDotnetProject now places compatible projects into shared restore and build groups to avoid repeated restores, and volume mounts accept an env argument so apps read one environment variable for data path locally and after deployment.
insights.speaker: Almir Vuk
insights.so_what: Build-time and local/deployed parity improvements reduce inner-loop friction.
